The equipment must be used primarily for customs controls but may also be used for additional purposes, including national border management and investigation.

The Instrument will support the achievement of an adequate and equivalent level of customs control results at the Union's external borders, enabling the benefits of the customs union to be maximized. The dedicated Union fund for customs control equipment will contribute to the overall cohesion between Member States and take into account the different needs experienced at various types of borders. The Commission will encourage joint procurement and joint testing of customs control equipment by two or more Member States. Costs incurred in respect of actions supported under this Regulation may, for a limited period, be considered eligible from January 1, 2021, even if those actions were implemented and costs incurred before the grant application was submitted. The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts to update the indicative list of customs control equipment, ensuring that the Instrument remains effective in supporting the customs union and customs authorities.

The Fund aims to contribute to the development of the Common European Asylum System, strengthen legal migration, counter irregular migration, and enhance solidarity among Member States. To achieve these objectives, the Fund will support various actions, including specific actions, Union actions, emergency assistance, resettlement, and humanitarian admission. The Fund will also provide support for the transfer of applicants for international protection and for the European Migration Network. 

The Fund is open to participation from third countries that have concluded an agreement with the Union on asylum and migration. Such agreements must ensure cooperation in the areas of asylum, migration, and return, and be underpinned by principles of non-refoulement, democracy, and respect for human rights. The agreements must also ensure a fair balance of contributions and benefits, and provide for the necessary rights and access for Union institutions to ensure sound financial management.

The allocation of funding from the Fund will be based on specific criteria, including the progress made by Member States in achieving milestones and addressing identified shortcomings in implementation. The Fund will also support technical assistance and training activities, and will monitor progress through various indicators, including the number of participants in training activities, the number of persons resettled, and the number of persons admitted through humanitarian admission.

In order to receive additional funding, Member States must demonstrate that they have made significant progress in implementing their programmes, and that at least 90% of their initial allocation has been covered by payment applications. The Commission will review the progress of Member States in 2024 and allocate additional funding accordingly. The Fund will also support actions that promote the integration of third-country nationals, including measures implemented by local and regional authorities and civil society organisations, and actions that develop and implement effective alternatives to detention. 

Overall, the Fund aims to promote a comprehensive and coordinated approach to migration and asylum, and to support Member States in their efforts to manage migration challenges and promote the integration of third-country nationals. The Fund's activities will be guided by a set of core performance indicators, which will be used to monitor progress and evaluate the effectiveness of the Fund's actions. These indicators will include data on the number of persons transferred, resettled, or admitted through humanitarian admission, as well as data on the support provided to vulnerable persons and applicants for international protection.

The Asylum, Migration and Integration Fund, established for the period from 1 January 2021 to 31 December 2027, aims to contribute to several specific objectives, including strengthening and developing the Common European Asylum System, promoting legal migration, countering irregular migration, and enhancing solidarity and fair sharing of responsibility between Member States. The Fund will support actions such as specific actions, Union actions, emergency assistance, resettlement and humanitarian admission, and support to Member States for the transfer of applicants for international protection or beneficiaries of international protection. 

To be eligible to be associated with the Fund, a third country must have concluded an agreement with the Union on the criteria and mechanisms for establishing the State responsible for examining a request for asylum. The agreement covering the participation of the third country in the Fund must enable cooperation with the Member States and the Union institutions, be underpinned by principles such as non-refoulement, democracy, and respect for human rights, and ensure a fair balance as regards contributions and benefits. The agreement must also lay down the conditions of participation, including the calculation of financial contributions, and guarantee the rights of the Union to ensure sound financial management.

The Fund will be allocated flexibly through a thematic facility, which will primarily serve internal Union policy. The allocation of funds will take into account the progress made by Member States in achieving milestones and identified shortcomings in implementation. The Commission will review the Fund's performance mid-term, in 2024, and allocate additional funds to Member States based on their performance. Member States that have not covered at least 10% of their initial allocation by payment applications will not be eligible to receive additional allocations. The Fund's performance will be measured through result indicators, including the number of participants in training activities, the number of participants who received pre-departure support, and the number of applicants for and beneficiaries of international protection transferred from one Member State to another. 

The Union budget may contribute up to 90% of the total eligible expenditure for certain actions, and Member States are encouraged to pursue actions eligible for higher co-financing rates. The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts to amend the list of actions eligible for higher co-financing rates in response to unforeseen circumstances or to ensure effective implementation of funding. Overall, the Asylum, Migration and Integration Fund aims to support the development of a comprehensive and effective asylum and migration policy in the European Union, while promoting solidarity and cooperation between Member States and third countries.

The Fund aims to contribute to the strengthening and development of the Common European Asylum System, as well as to the development of legal migration and the effective integration of third-country nationals. It also seeks to counter irregular migration, enhance return and readmission procedures, and promote solidarity and fair sharing of responsibility between Member States. To achieve these objectives, the Fund will support a range of activities, including specific actions, Union actions, emergency assistance, and resettlement and humanitarian admission programs. The Fund will also provide support for the transfer of applicants for international protection and for the European Migration Network.

The Fund is open to participation from third countries, provided they have concluded an agreement with the Union on the criteria and mechanisms for establishing the State responsible for examining a request for asylum. Such agreements must ensure cooperation in the areas of asylum, migration, and return, and must be underpinned by principles of non-refoulement, democracy, the rule of law, and respect for human rights. The agreements must also ensure a fair balance between the contributions made by and the benefits received by the participating third country.

The Commission will allocate funding from the Fund to Member States through a thematic facility, which will support a range of activities, including those related to asylum, migration, and integration. The allocation of funding will take into account the progress made by Member States in achieving the milestones of the performance framework and identified shortcomings in implementation. A mid-term review will be conducted in 2024 to assess the effectiveness of the Fund and to allocate additional funding to Member States that have made significant progress in achieving the objectives of the Fund.

The Fund will also support training activities, pre-departure support, and the transfer of applicants for international protection between Member States. The Commission will monitor the implementation of the Fund and will carry out a mid-term evaluation to assess its effectiveness, efficiency, relevance, coherence, and Union added value. The Commission may also make observations on amendments to programs submitted by Member States and may carry out assessments of the compliance of such amendments with the relevant regulations. Overall, the Fund aims to promote a comprehensive and coordinated approach to asylum, migration, and integration, and to support the development of a fair and effective Common European Asylum System.

This Regulation aims to support the development of trans-European networks in the transport, energy, and digital sectors. To achieve this goal, the Commission will provide technical assistance to Member States that are eligible for funding from the Cohesion Fund, particularly those that face difficulties in designing projects with sufficient maturity, quality, and Union added value. The Commission will also give special attention to Member States with a gross national income per capita of less than 60% of the EU-27 average, to help them absorb the available funds.

In the transport sector, eligible actions for funding include the development of efficient, interconnected, and multimodal networks, such as railway, road, inland waterway, and maritime infrastructure. This includes actions implementing the core network, cross-border links, and missing links, as well as urban nodes, multimodal logistics platforms, and maritime ports. Additionally, actions supporting smart, interoperable, sustainable, and inclusive mobility, such as motorways of the sea, telematic applications, and sustainable freight transport services, are also eligible.

In the energy sector, eligible actions include projects of common interest, such as cross-border projects in the field of renewable energy, including innovative solutions and storage of renewable energy. In the digital sector, eligible actions include the deployment of and access to very high capacity networks, including 5G systems, as well as actions supporting the provision of very high-quality local wireless connectivity in local communities.

The Commission will regularly assess the uptake of funds for cross-border projects in the field of renewable energy and, if necessary, reallocate unused budget to meet the objectives of the trans-European energy networks. Priority for funding will be determined based on criteria such as the deployment of very high capacity networks, the provision of local wireless connectivity, and the deployment of 5G corridors along major transport paths.

Overall, this Regulation aims to promote the development of trans-European networks, enhance the competitiveness of the EU, and support the achievement of the Union's strategic objectives, including the transition to a low-carbon economy and the promotion of digitalization and innovation.

Additionally, actions that remove barriers to interoperability, improve transport infrastructure resilience and accessibility, and support new technologies and innovation are eligible for funding.

In the energy sector, eligible actions include projects of common interest, such as those set out in Regulation (EU) No 347/2013, and cross-border projects in the field of renewable energy, including innovative solutions and storage of renewable energy. In the digital sector, eligible actions include those supporting the deployment of and access to very high capacity networks, including 5G systems, and the provision of very high-quality local wireless connectivity in local communities.
